observation.summary: This change only renames a private helper in src/theseus_reviewer/dedup.py, from _normalise to _normalised_title, and updates its one call site in fingerprint(). The helper body is unchanged. So is the hashed string f"{path}\n{normalised title}" and the 16-character truncation, which means fingerprint() returns the same value for every input before and after the change. Bypass scenarios checked: (1) A changed fingerprint could stop duplicate findings from collapsing, or make distinct findings collide and drop one. Ruled out because the hash input and algorithm are identical. (2) A caller of the old name would break at runtime and could turn the dedup step into an error path. Ruled out because a grep of the whole workspace for `_normalise` as a whole word found no other references. The only dedup consumer found is tests/unit/reviewer/test_dedup.py, and it uses only the public fingerprint(). (3) The change does not touch reviewer selection, thresholds, verdict parsing or error handling, so it cannot steer reviews or weaken scrutiny. (4) No test was added or changed, so the test-hygiene and network-faking rules do not apply.

findings.detail: The test calls monkeypatch.setattr(github.subprocess, "run", fake_run). This patches the standard-library subprocess.run globally, not a boundary that theseus_reviewer.github owns. If download_state is refactored, for example to `from subprocess import run`, Popen, or a call through _gh, the fake is bypassed and the unit test runs the real `gh run download 7 --repo o/r` over the network. Fix: give download_state an injectable runner, or a module-level function in github.py that the test patches, and fake that instead. See the same problem at line 47 in test_a_failed_download_yields_no_state.
findings.title: Stdlib subprocess.run patched: in test_a_downloaded_state_artifact_is_read

findings.detail: The test calls monkeypatch.setattr(github.subprocess, "run", failing_run), patching the standard-library subprocess.run instead of a boundary owned by github.py. If a refactor bypasses this fake, the test calls the real `gh` CLI against GitHub. That real call would most likely fail as well, so download_state would still return None and the test would keep passing silently: it would reach the network and verify nothing. Fix: fake an injectable runner or a module-owned function in github.py, as for line 38 in test_a_downloaded_state_artifact_is_read.
findings.title: Stdlib subprocess.run patched: in test_a_failed_download_yields_no_state

observation.summary: The change adds two unit tests for theseus_reviewer.github.download_state. Both fake the external `gh run download` call by monkeypatching `github.subprocess.run`. `github.subprocess` is the standard-library subprocess module itself, so each test replaces the stdlib `subprocess.run` for the whole process instead of using a boundary the module owns. The reviewer module owns no such boundary today: download_state calls subprocess.run directly, with no injectable runner. Both _gh and download_state call `subprocess.run` through the module attribute, so the patch intercepts them for now. A refactor would silently bypass the fake: for example `from subprocess import run`, routing download_state through _gh, or switching to Popen or check_output. The tests would then run the real `gh` CLI against GitHub (repo o/r, run 7) from a unit test. In the failure test the real call would almost certainly fail too and return None, so it would keep passing while verifying nothing. Monkeypatch restores the attribute, so no process-global state leaks after the test. Nothing outside tests changes, so no gate, selection, threshold or verdict-parsing path is altered. Bypass scenarios considered: no sound

findings.detail: The test used to compare the whole secrets dict with the expected mapping. It now checks values for only 4 of the 7 secrets. TS_OAUTH_CI_CLIENT_ID, TS_OAUTH_CI_SECRET and TYPESAFE_API_KEY are checked only by name, not by value. A caller that maps one of them to the wrong or a wrong-environment secret would pass. The change gives no reason for the narrowing, and SECRET_SOURCES still lists all 7 entries.
findings.title: Secret mapping check narrowed in test_every_caller_secret_maps_to_the_secret_it_is_named_for

findings.detail: The two 'edited' cases were deleted. review-gate.yml still triggers on issue_comment 'edited' and still has the clause `github.event.action == 'edited' && contains(github.event.changes.body.from, 'Stand-in review')`. That clause is no longer exercised. The test's _matches helper reimplements the logic in Python and only asserts that a substring is present in the condition. It never evaluates the real expression, so it could not detect a regression in the edited path anyway. Removing the cases takes the edited path (turning a stand-in marker comment into something else, or the reverse) out of coverage. That is a gate-bypass vector.
findings.title: Edited-comment gate cases removed from CONDITION_CASES while review-gate.yml still has the edited clause

observation.summary: The diff only weakens tests and touches no production code. It removes coverage of the review-gate trigger and of secret mapping. Bypass scenarios I could not rule out: (1) a future PR drops or alters the 'edited' clause in review-gate.yml and no test notices; (2) a future PR rewires TS_OAUTH_CI_CLIENT_ID, TS_OAUTH_CI_SECRET or TYPESAFE_API_KEY to a different secret and the test still passes.

I read both changed files in full, plus .github/review.yml and .github/soundness-paths.txt to check the gate wiring. The change adds an optional `forced` parameter to `judge()` in src/theseus_reviewer/protocol.py, defaulting to False. When it is True, a prior that the author disputed and the reviewer marked FIXED is treated as NOT_FIXED, so it is published as MAINTAINED and counts toward escalation. This can only make a review stricter. Bypass scenarios I considered: (1) Weakened verdicts: the only new path turns FIXED into MAINTAINED, never the other way, so no finding can be dropped or downgraded. (2) A concession overriding the forced round: the check `prior.id in disputed and prior.concedes` still runs first and still yields WITHDRAWN. The base code behaved the same, so the forced round adds no new route to withdraw a finding. (3) Default behaviour: `forced` defaults to False and no caller in this repository passes it, so every existing `judge()` call and the escalation in `escalates()` behave exactly as at the base commit. (4) Soundness coverage and selection: the gate_paths in review.yml and the `src/theseus_reviewer/` prefix in soundness-paths.txt are unchanged. Nothing in t

findings.detail: `if selection.load_tokens and not (resolution is not None and resolution.substituted)` turns off both capacity checks whenever a fallback model is substituted. Example: load_tokens=600, capacities={'small': 400}, fallback window 1000. The primary path skips this reviewer, but the substituted path accepts it, so a slot that accepts 400 tokens reviews a 600-token change. That can mean a truncated or partial review. In the same way, capacities={} with capacity_error='catalog unreadable' used to fail closed; with a substitution it now passes. A model's context window is not the reviewer slot's accepted capacity. Only the substituted path is weakened, and it is the path where the primary model is down. The slot capacity and the unknown-capacity checks must also apply to substituted resolutions.
findings.title: Capacity gate bypass: substituted resolution skips slot capacity and unknown-capacity checks in skip_reason

findings.detail: next_reviewer calls `reason, _ = skip_reason(...)` and returns only the Reviewer. The resolved target model and the substituted flag are lost. A caller that runs the returned reviewer will use its primary model, which resolve has just found is not served. Even if some fallback does run, the result cannot record which model actually did the review, so the review is unverifiable. next_reviewer must return the Resolution, or the chosen model, together with the reviewer so that the substitution is applied and recorded.
findings.title: Resolution dropped: next_reviewer discards substituted target

findings.detail: The only substitution test uses load_tokens=300 with slot capacity 400, so the test passes whether or not substitution skips the capacity gate. No test covers a substituted resolution with load above the slot capacity, or with an unknown capacity. None of the tests exercise next_reviewer with availability=True, so the dropped resolution in next_reviewer also goes unnoticed. Together these let the two defects above ship.
findings.title: Test gap: fallback test cannot detect capacity bypass in test_a_served_fallback_runs_when_the_primary_is_not_served

observation.summary: I read every changed file in full: selection.py and test_selection.py. I also read providers.py and capacity.py, which the change depends on, and searched the repository for callers of skip_reason and next_reviewer. The only callers are in the tests. I checked five ways a defect could get past the gate. (1) Unknown candidates or no served model: resolve returns target None, so the reviewer is skipped. That fails closed and is safe. (2) A missing window entry defaults to 0, so a large change is never sent to a model with an unknown window. Safe. (3) Substitution skips the slot capacity check and the check for an unreadable capacity catalog. A reviewer slot can then review a change larger than it accepts, or run when its capacity is unknown. This can happen, so it is a defect. (4) next_reviewer throws away the Resolution. The model that is chosen is not passed to the run, so the substituted model may never be used, and the record cannot show which model reviewed the change. This can happen, so it is a defect.
